_description: CATALOG CORRECTIONS LAYER. Corrects any field the pipeline derives from m4b tags - title, author, narrator, year, genre, series, series_index - without touching the audio files. Read by app/core/catalog_overrides.py, applied by app/metadata.py:extract_metadata() after tag extraction and title parsing. The correction is always the last word.
_why_this_exists: site/catalog.csv is a generated copy (app/main.py step 3). Editing it is wiped by the next build. Every value in it comes from the m4b tags, and a large part of this library was tagged by hand over several years, so the tags carry hand-entry damage: blanks, four spellings of one series name, volume numbers off by one, series fields holding the book title. This file is where that damage is corrected. It is not a pile of exceptions - it is the corrected truth for this catalog, and it is expected to grow to cover the whole library.
_precedent: Shape and location follow scripts/author_aliases.json and scripts/author_shelf_aliases.json. Unlike those, every entry is evidence-bearing: each corrected field must carry an evidence note saying what was on disk and what settled it, and tests/test_catalog_overrides.py fails the build if one does not. A future reader must always be able to tell a researched correction from a typo.
_relationship_to_the_tag_sweep: This layer leaves the m4b files alone, so it is safe and instant but only fixes the catalog. app/tools/audit_series_tags.py is the other half: it surveys the real tags across all 422 author folders and can write corrections back into the files (dry run by default, --commit to write, sidecar backup first). Run the survey, decide, then either fix the tags at source or record the correction here. Entries here stay valid either way - a corrected tag simply makes its entry redundant rather than wrong.

_schema.match: An entry applies when EVERY field present in its match block matches the extracted metadata. See _keying below.
_schema.match.asin: Audible product ASIN, from the CDEK atom. The most stable key - survives both file renames and retagging. Absent on hand-tagged files.
_schema.match.title: Matched against the ©nam tag, case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed.
_schema.match.author: Matches if this name is one of the comma-separated names in the extracted author field, case-insensitive.
_schema.match.file: Basename of the m4b, case-insensitive. Use only to disambiguate; it does not survive a rename.
_schema.set: Field -> corrected value. Allowed fields: title, author, narrator, year, genre, series, series_index. Set series_index to "" to force the volume BLANK when the true number is unknown - never invent one.
_schema.evidence: Required. Must contain one key per field in 'set', explaining that specific correction. May also carry 'tags_read', 'filename_said', 'sources' and 'note'. 'sources' holds citable URLs when the value came from outside the files.
_schema.added: ISO date the entry was added.
_schema.canonical_series: variant spelling (lowercased) -> canonical spelling. Applied to EVERY book after extraction, whether or not an entry matched. This is what stops one series being spelled four ways.

_keying.problem: Both of the obvious keys drift. Filenames get renamed by hand and by the sort scripts; tags get rewritten by re-downloads, by OpenAudible, and by the eventual tag sweep.
_keying.rule: Key on ASIN when the file has one - it is the product identity and survives both kinds of drift. Otherwise key on title + author, which survives renames and re-syncs (a re-download restores the same ©nam/©ART) and only breaks if someone deliberately retitles the book. Use 'file' only as a tiebreaker for genuinely ambiguous titles, never as the sole key.
_keying.consequence: The hand-made files that need correcting most - Completionist Chronicles 8-14 - have no ASIN at all, so those entries are keyed on title + author. If the tag sweep later writes ASINs into them, add the asin field to those entries and they become rename-proof and retag-proof.

_verified: 2026-08-11. Every 'tags_read' value was read from the real m4b with mutagen. Every volume number was cross-checked against a citable external source as well as the file's own tags; where the two disagree the disagreement is written down rather than smoothed over.

_precedence_rule.finding: Across all 14 Completionist Chronicles books the trkn tag was correct every single time. The FILENAMES were the damaged source: one had no series at all, one claimed the wrong volume, one had the book title in the series slot, and the series name was spelled four ways. There was never a real volume collision.
_precedence_rule.rule: Where a tag and a filename disagree, PREFER THE TAG and treat the filename as suspect. Filename parsing is evidence to report, never a value to write over a good tag. app/parsers/title.py only runs when the tags are silent, and it must stay that way.
_precedence_rule.consequence: The damage is narrower than it looked. Ordering never needs reconstructing - only the series STRING is broken. That makes both this layer and the eventual tag sweep much lower risk than assumed.

_not_corrected_on_purpose.Completionist Chronicles books 1-7: Ritualist, Regicide, Rexus: Side Quest, Raze, Ruthless, Inflame and Invent were downloaded from Audible and still carry their vendor tags (SRNM='The Completionist Chronicles', SRSQ=1..7, plus CDEK ASINs and an SRLK series link). They already appear correctly in the catalog and need no entry. Their FILENAMES spell the series four different ways - with and without 'The', with and without 'Series' - but a filename never reaches the series field while SRNM is present, so that is cosmetic. canonical_series above catches it if the vendor tags are ever lost, and the tag sweep will report it.
_not_corrected_on_purpose.verified_run: With the seven entries above, the Completionist Chronicles run is complete and contiguous, 1 through 14, no gaps and no duplicate volumes - matching the Goodreads series listing exactly and the owner's expectation of ~14 books.

_not_owned._why_this_is_here: So that a future audit does not read these as missing data and try to manufacture entries for them. They are genuine gaps in what the owner has bought, not defects in the catalog.

The Completionist Chronicles.note: Four decimal-numbered short stories listed by Goodreads and not present in the library. Do NOT create override entries for them.
